subject: religious-studies
title: Kant's Categorical Imperative and Applied Ethics
welcome_lead: Walk the streets of Konigsberg with Immanuel Kant as he grounds morality in the rational will and its categorical demands.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Kantian deontology, the three formulations of the categorical imperative, and applications to medical and sexual ethics.
final_note: You have followed Kant's argument from autonomy through universalisability to the Kingdom of Ends.

concepts.def: For Kant, the only thing good without qualification; the will that acts from duty alone.
An unconditional command of reason, binding on all rational agents regardless of desire.
A conditional command of the form 'if you want X, do Y'.
Act only on that maxim by which you can will it should become a universal law.
Treat humanity, whether in your own person or another's, always as an end and never merely as a means.
An ideal community in which all rational agents legislate universal laws for one another as ends in themselves.

walkthroughs.body_html: Kant opens the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785): 'Nothing in the world can be conceived as good without qualification except a good will.' Acting from inclination, even kindly, has no moral worth. Only acting from duty, out of respect for the moral law, gives an action moral content.

Kant presents the Categorical Imperative in several formulations he claims are equivalent. (1) The Universal Law: universalise your maxim. (2) The Humanity formula: never use persons merely as means. (3) The Kingdom of Ends: act as a legislator in a community of rational ends. Lying to a murderer, Kant notoriously insists, fails the universalisability test.

Kantian ethics opposes euthanasia on the grounds that taking one's life treats one's rational nature as a mere means to escape suffering. In sexual ethics, Kant in his Lectures on Ethics argues that sexual desire risks reducing the other to a thing; he believed marriage's juridical structure prevents this. Modern Kantians like Korsgaard reinterpret these conclusions more permissively.

mcqs.q: Which is the Humanity Formula of the Categorical Imperative?
options: Act only on universalisable maxims
Treat humanity never merely as a means but always as an end
Act so as to maximise happiness
Act as if your will were lawgiver in a Kingdom of Ends

mcqs.q: For Kant, the only thing good without qualification is:
options: Pleasure
Virtue
A good will
Knowledge

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.
Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
